results.message: What did Augustine say about Psalm 137, dashing the little ones against the rock?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
Augustine says the little ones of Babylon are bad desires at their birth, and we must dash them on the Rock, who is Christ: “How shall they repay her? As she has treated us. Let her little ones be choked in their turn. Yes, let her little ones in their turn be dashed, and die. What are the little ones of Babylon? Evil desires at their birth. For some people have to fight with old, deep-rooted cravings. When a craving is born, evil habit has not yet given it strength against you. While it is little, do not let it gain the strength of evil habit. While it is little, dash it. But you fear that, though dashed, it may not die. “Dash it against the Rock; and that Rock is Christ.””

He was teaching those being formed for baptism. He did not soften what the psalm said, and he did not leave it as a command to literal violence. He named Babylon as the confusion of this world, where bad desires are born in us. The little ones are those desires while they are still small, before they grow strong enough to master you. The Rock is Christ. To dash them against him is to bring those desires, while they are still weak, to the one who can kill them. That is what the psalm is telling you to do.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV, independently re-located this session; Doc_01 SS2); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII; Doc_01 SS2); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo (lpc.story.the-psalms-on-the-wall)

confidence.divergence_note: The text field is the NPNF English as printed. Augustine comments on the Latin Psalter, where Psalm 136 ends 'Blessed is he who shall hold and dash thy little ones against the rock'. 'Choked' renders offocentur, 'be smothered', and 'dashed' renders elidantur, 'be struck down'. The closing words echo 1 Corinthians 10:4, which the Latin cites.
